title: Debugging Data-Type Errors
keywords: errors, debugging, testing, and code quality
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of debugging data-type errors and name one situation where it is useful.
Apply unexpected inferred types to a small NumPy example and inspect the resulting values, shape, or dtype.
Identify one important limitation, boundary case, or validation check for debugging data-type errors.

content.intro: This lesson develops topic 184 of the supplied curriculum: **Debugging Data-Type Errors**. The main starting point is **Unexpected inferred types**. You will connect the idea to a small, synthetic example, then use the result to reason about shape, dtype, accuracy, or memory as appropriate.
content.why_it_matters: Reliable numerical code makes failures reproducible and tests the invariants that matter: shape, dtype, finite values, exact results where appropriate, and tolerances for approximate results.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Treat **Debugging Data-Type Errors** as an explicit step in an array workflow. This lesson centers on **Unexpected inferred types** and the source syllabus's related subtopics. Before trusting a result, identify the input shape and dtype, perform the smallest useful operation, and inspect the output. The example uses synthetic data so you can change one value and observe what changes.

common_mistakes.problem: Testing approximate values with strict equality
common_mistakes.why: Numerical methods can legitimately introduce small rounding differences.
Empty inputs, invalid types, shape mismatch, and NaN may reveal defects.
common_mistakes.fix: Add explicit boundary and invalid-input tests.
